messages:
zara: Hey all, first week hiccup. I'm in GitHub Codespaces (devcontainer) and mounted the kubeconfig from onboarding to `~/.kube/config` but `kubectl get ns` fails with: `error: dial tcp: lookup api.dev.redwood.internal: no such host`. Looks like DNS fail inside Codespace. Anyone seen this?

thiago: Welcome Zara! Codespaces run outside our VPC so internal DNS names like `*.dev.redwood.internal` won't resolve. Two options: 1) use our dev-tunnel proxy (devex) that forwards cluster DNS, 2) SSH into the bastion and run commands from there.

zara: dev-tunnel? I couldn't find it in the onboarding doc. Is it self-service?

infra-bot: Dev-tunnel is self-service for approved users. Docs: https://intranet.redwood.ai/devex/dev-tunnel. It requires a short-lived token and the `dev-tunnel` CLI installed in the container. If you prefer SSH, request `bastion-ssh` access.

zara: I tried installing `dev-tunnel` but it errors with `401 unauthorized` when trying to start. I guess I don't have the token yet.

thiago: If you need quick access for debugging, easiest is to request bastion access for 1 day in the Access Portal and then `ssh -J jumpbox.internal redwood@jumpbox` and run `kubectl` there. For longer term Codespaces, we usually run `dev-tunnel start --env dev` in the devcontainer.

zara: Filed a one-day bastion request in the portal and pinged infra. PR link also created: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4502 (temp bastion access).

ops-bot: Access request created: infra PR #4502 by zara. Reviewer: jen. Reminder: bastion access requires 2FA.

jen: Approved the temporary bastion access for zara. Applied at 1799998075. You should be able to `ssh jumpbox.redwood.internal` now.

infra-bot: RBAC change applied by jen at 1799998075 (bastion-ssh for 1d).

zara: SSHed into jumpbox and ran `kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/config get ns` and it works now. Thanks! Quick follow-up: while on jumpbox I tried `kubectl get pods -n infra-staging` and got `Forbidden`. I need read access to infra-staging from Codespaces for debugging. What's the recommended flow?

thiago: For devcontainers we don't hand out long-lived user creds. We prefer two approaches: 1) create a namespaced ServiceAccount `sa: zara-codespace` with `view` role and bind it for the `infra-staging` namespace (short expiry), or 2) add your user to the `infra-developers` group with time-limited access. Both require an access request PR.

zara: Which is faster? I don't want a lot of manual steps in the devcontainer.

jen: ServiceAccount is faster for Codespaces: infra can create SA + RoleBinding and provide the kubeconfig snippet to mount in the container. I can do that for 7 days if you include a justification in the PR. Please open a PR in infra/access-requests with the YAML and tag me. Example snippet we need in PR description:

```
- requester: zara
  requested_for: serviceaccount
  namespace: infra-staging
  role: view
  duration: 7d
  reason: debugging app crash from Codespaces
```

zara: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4503 with that exact body.

infra-bot: New access request PR #4503 created by zara (serviceaccount request). CI checks passed.

jen: Approved and applied. Created `zara-codespace` serviceaccount in `infra-staging` with a 7d expiry and posted the kubeconfig snippet to the PR.

ops-bot: ServiceAccount kubeconfig snippet available in PR #4503 comments. Remember to delete local copies after use.

zara: Pulled the kubeconfig snippet into the Codespace at `~/.kube/code-sa-config` and `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/code-sa-config kubectl get pods -n infra-staging` now returns a list. Everything working now. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:
